Number of studies.evidence_source: Sentences indicating a single repeated-measures study: "Multilevel modeling ... was used to test our hypotheses. Multilevel modeling is the preferred approach when examining hierarchical data sets such as this one in which assessment days (level-1) were nested within participants (level-2)."

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the analytic strategy for a single repeated-measures study using multilevel modeling (days nested within participants) with maximum likelihood estimation. It explains creation of between-person (person means) and two kinds of within-person predictors (daily deviations from person mean and day-to-day difference/lag variables), and two sets of multilevel models: one examining within-day and across-week effects (with BMI and mean exposures as level-2 covariates) and one examining day-to-day changes (with lagged criterion variables and BMI as covariate). The section does not label any study as 'Study 1' or report sample demographics or measurement instruments.
section_summary.evidence_source: "Between-persons (level-2) predictors were created by taking the mean of participants' scores on the variable in question across days of the study." "Two sets of within-person (level-1) predictor variables were calculated..." "Hypotheses were tested with two series of multilevel models."
